protocol.route_order: Four routes rotate by workload and reverse on alternate rounds; five rounds.

protocol.frame_quantiles: Sorted 320 raw frame durations per process; index (len-1)*percentile//100. Summary times are medians of five process quantiles.

protocol.best_cpu_selection: Choose fixed admitted CPU requested route post-hoc by median of its five frame medians; preserve its actual route and every paired alternative.

interpretation: Dense Interpreter uses the current checked Rust packet. Dense native requests commit real SIMD lanes.
Density1 and routed SIMD requests execute scalar native tails; no SIMD speed claim is made for these cases.
Immutable advance is faster than the selected best CPU alternative in all five paired workload medians, but public full/selected queries regress.
Density1 medians 167ns versus 208ns differ by approximately one 41.7ns timer quantum; this is a timer-quantized small-workload observation, not a statistical significance claim.
Full and selected query workloads differ: 14 fields versus Position+Rotation for density, Rotation alone for routed; each query observation contains eight sweeps.
These Delta-dependent outputs retain CPU query/transport work; no WGSL offload or end-to-end rendering gain was measured.
Constant-rate Delta closure does not replace variable-step Euler with continuous acceleration; no constant-acceleration family is included.
No acquired native effect applicability gain is established by these synthetic controls.
